name: Lérins Press
tagline: The publishing arm of Mere Catholicity

motto.latin: Quod ubique, quod semper, quod ab omnibus creditum est.
motto.english: What has been believed everywhere, always, and by all.

about: Lérins is a small island off the coast of Cannes. Early in the fifth century Honoratus founded a monastery there, and it became a school for the Church in Gaul. Bishops came out of it, Hilary of Arles, Eucherius of Lyon, Lupus of Troyes and Caesarius of Arles among them, and so did books.

One of its monks, Vincent, wrote a short book in 434 for telling the faith of the Church from the novelties pressed on it. His rule is the one this house takes its name from. Hold to what has been believed everywhere, always, and by all.
Lérins Press is the publishing arm of merecatholicity.com. It publishes the books written there, and in time careful editions of the classics the site already keeps free to read online.

originals.name: Lérins Originals
about: Books from Lérins Press that stand in none of its collections.

collections.name: Lérins Newman
collections.tagline: The works of John Henry Newman, Anglican and Catholic
about: John Henry Newman (1801 to 1890) lived forty-four years in the Church of England and forty-five in the Catholic Church, and wrote through both. At Oxford he led the movement that called the Church of England back to the Fathers. Reading them, he came to believe that their Church was the Church of Rome, and in 1845 he was received into it. He died a cardinal, and was canonized in 2019.

He argued with Vincent of Lérins all his life: how the faith held everywhere, always and by all can grow without becoming something else. Lérins Newman prints his works in three parts, the Anglican years, the Catholic years, and the essays, sketches and verse he gathered late in life, numbered in that order, so each book shows where it stands in one life.

collections.name: Lérins Fathers
collections.tagline: The Fathers of the Church, one work at a time
about: The Fathers are the Church's first teachers after the apostles: the bishops, martyrs and monks who received the faith, defended it and handed it on. Vincent of Lérins, whose island gives this press its name, held that what they taught together, everywhere and always, is the faith itself.

Lérins Fathers prints their works one at a time, from the Didache and Ignatius to John of Damascus, with the monks of the desert and the first historian of the Church among them, and after them the Golden Chain, the Gospels expounded in the Fathers' own words.

collections.name: Lérins Devotions
collections.tagline: The great books of the devotional life
about: The books Christians have prayed with for sixteen centuries: Augustine's Confessions, written as one long prayer, the English mystics, the Imitation of Christ, Teresa of Ávila and John of the Cross, Francis de Sales and Brother Lawrence, William Law, Thérèse of Lisieux and A. W. Tozer.
Lérins Devotions prints them to be read slowly and kept close.

collections.name: Lérins Reformation
collections.tagline: The Reformers, the Puritans and their heirs, in their own words
about: The Reformation and its heirs in their own voice: The Reformed Catholic Reader, Calvin and the teachers of Mercersburg on the Church and the sacraments, then Luther and Calvin’s Institutes, the English Puritans, Sibbes, Baxter, Owen, Watson and Bunyan, and Spurgeon, who read them all his life.
Each claimed the old paths, the Scriptures and the Fathers. Lérins Reformation prints them whole, in their own words, so the reader may judge.

collections.name: Lérins America
collections.tagline: The Great Awakening and the Founding, in the original texts
about: The revival preached by Jonathan Edwards and George Whitefield, and the republic argued into being by Paine, Jefferson, Adams, Madison, Hamilton and their opponents, in the documents themselves.
Lérins America prints them whole, each in the words its first readers had.

collections.name: Lérins Schoolhouse
collections.tagline: The old American schoolbooks, for the teacher at home
about: The books American children learned from in the one-room schoolhouse: Webster's Blue-Backed Speller, McGuffey's Eclectic Readers and Ray's Arithmetic, each whole, as the schools used them.
Lérins Schoolhouse sets them large, with a new introduction for the teacher, guides to their old sounds and measures, and answer keys to their exercises.

collections.name: Lérins Chesterton
collections.tagline: G. K. Chesterton in four volumes, two books to a volume
about: G. K. Chesterton (1874 to 1936) was a journalist, poet, novelist and critic, the author of Orthodoxy and The Everlasting Man and of the Father Brown stories. He was received into the Catholic Church in 1922.

Lérins Chesterton prints his prose argument in four volumes of two books each: Heretics · Orthodoxy, The Everlasting Man · The Thing, What’s Wrong with the World · The Outline of Sanity, and the essays, Tremendous Trifles · All Things Considered.

collections.name: Lérins MacDonald
about: George MacDonald (1824 to 1905), a Scottish Congregational minister who left the pulpit for the pen, wrote fairy tales and fantasies, novels of Scottish life, poems and three series of Unspoken Sermons. C. S. Lewis named him his master, and G. K. Chesterton counted him among the great writers of his age.

Lérins MacDonald prints his chief books in four volumes: Phantastes · Lilith, the three series of Unspoken Sermons, At the Back of the North Wind · Dealings with the Fairies, and The Princess and the Goblin · The Princess and Curdie.

collections.name: Lérins Classics
collections.tagline: The great books, from Homer to Faulkner
about: The great books, from Homer and Plato to Hemingway and Faulkner: the epics and the plays, the philosophers, and the novels every list of the greatest books names.
Lérins Classics prints each whole, in its own words or in a translation of standing, with a new introduction and notes for the reader of today.

privacy: Lérins Press, the publishing arm of merecatholicity.com, keeps as little about you as it can. This site has no ads, no analytics and no tracking cookies, and you need no account to read it.

If you join the mailing list, we keep your email address, the date you joined and the wording you agreed to, and nothing else. We use the address only to tell you of new books and of the press's news. We never sell, rent or trade it, and never give it to anyone to market to you. If you write to us through the contact page, your name, email address and message reach the editors by email and are kept only in that mailbox.

Every email from the list will carry a way to leave it. You may also enter your address in the form on the home page and press Unsubscribe, and the address is deleted from the list, not merely marked. To ask what we hold about you, or to have it corrected or deleted, write to us through the contact page.

The site, the list's database and its bot check run on Cloudflare, which, like any web host, may log your IP address. Cloudflare Turnstile checks that a form is sent by a person and not a program. Email to the list will go out through a mail provider that receives only the addresses and the message. The books are sold by Amazon under its own terms and privacy notice, and we receive nothing about you from a sale.

Otherwise we disclose information only when the law requires it, or to protect the press, its readers or others from fraud or harm. If the press passes to new hands, the list may pass with it, under this same policy. The press is based in the United States, and your information is stored and processed there and wherever its providers operate.

Everything travels over HTTPS and is kept with these providers in access-controlled accounts. No way of storing or sending information is perfectly secure, and we cannot promise that ours is. The site is not meant for children under thirteen, and we do not knowingly keep their information. If you believe a child has joined the list, tell us and we will delete the address.
We may change this policy at any time by posting the new version here, and it takes effect when posted. Last updated November 16, 2026.
